findings.note: The Anthropic effort-capable model table is wrong for three of its nine ids. The spec lists claude-opus-4-5, claude-opus-4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6 as taking output_config.effort for the full low|medium|high|xhigh vocabulary (spec 3.3 defines that vocabulary), and judge.go implements exactly that by writing body["output_config"] = {"effort": r.Effort} unconditionally for any capable id. Per the Anthropic API, effort on Opus 4.5 is limited to low/medium/high, and xhigh only arrived with Opus 4.7, so it is not accepted on Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6 either. A judge configured with any of those three ids at effort xhigh sends a body the API rejects with a 400. It fails closed (the 400 is mapped to ERR_JUDGE_EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED at judge.go:561) rather than misbehaving, which is why this is medium and not high, but the run is unrunnable in a configuration the table advertises as supported. Fix: make the table per-id effort sets, not one capable/legacy bit.

evidence.note: effort-capable list includes claude-opus-4-5, claude-opus-4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6 with no per-id effort ceiling
body["output_config"] = map[string]any{"effort": r.Effort} is written for every capable id with no xhigh guard
anthropicEffortCapable is a flat []string, so the model cannot carry a maximum supported effort

findings.note: Calibration mode is structurally impossible for two ids the same table declares supported. The spec pins calibration to thinking: {type: "disabled"} for every Anthropic model, and judge.go implements that as an unconditional branch taken before the family switch. claude-fable-5 and claude-mythos-5 have thinking always on and reject any explicit thinking configuration -- both {type: "disabled"} and {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N} return 400 -- so every calibration request against those two ids fails at the provider. The effort-capable list at spec line 158 names both, so nothing in the product refuses the combination earlier: judge.Preflight checks routing, key presence and the effort table only, and would let a fable-5 calibration run reach the network before failing. Fix: refuse calibration for always-thinking ids in Preflight, or omit the thinking key for them.

evidence.note: calibration is specified as thinking: {type: "disabled"} for the Anthropic provider with no per-family exception
case r.Calibration: body["thinking"] = {"type": "disabled"} runs before the capable/legacy switch, so it applies to fable-5 and mythos-5

findings.note: INSTALL.md's new prerequisite line documents a check that does not exist. It tells the reader that metareview fsm needs git >= 2.31 and that `metareview setup --check` reports it. setup.Check assembles Prerequisites from commandStatus PATH lookups only, and ToolStatus carries just Present/Path/Action -- there is no version probe for git anywhere in the repository (a repo-wide grep for 2.31 in Go sources returns nothing; the only hits are prose). commands/setup.md and skills/setup/SKILL.md likewise describe no version check. A user on git 2.28 gets a clean setup report and then a runtime failure in gate.Git.CommonDir, which is exactly the outcome the documented check is supposed to prevent. The spec's own ledger lists "git >= 2.31 in INSTALL + /setup" as a deliverable, so the INSTALL half shipped without the /setup half.

evidence.note: "metareview fsm needs git >= 2.31 (metareview setup --check reports it)" -- added by this diff
Git: commandStatus(lookup, "git", ...) is a bare PATH presence check; no version is executed or parsed
ToolStatus is {Present, Path, Action} -- the report has no field capable of carrying a version

findings.note: The Go floor is raised in INSTALL.md but left stale in two places the same branch touches. go.mod declares go 1.26, so a 1.22 toolchain cannot build the module at all, yet .claude-plugin/plugin.json's description -- a line this branch edits to append the FSM clause -- still reads "source checkout mode requires Go 1.22+", and setup.go's remediation string still says "Install Go 1.22+ and ensure go is on PATH". Both are user-facing.
